# Data

<!-- Describe input coverage, exclusions, units, and source versions with inline R. -->

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

# Analysis

## Prepare

Response, effort, index year and projected coordinates (km). Keep true zeros. With `EFFORT: "density"` the response is catch per swept area and there is no offset; with `EFFORT: "offset"` the response is catch and `log(swept_area)` enters as an offset. Either way predictions are made at offset 0, so they are densities per nmi², and `get_index(area =)` scales them once by the grid cell area. `year` is the **index year** (`INDEX_YEAR_START_MONTH`, `INDEX_YEAR_LABEL`); `calendar_year` keeps the survey year.

If Step 1 acquired a broader reporting polygon and added a `region` field, filter that field to the model-domain label here before constructing the mesh. Do not remove the broader stations during survey qualification or data compilation.

```{r prepare, eval=params$refit_model}
dt <- prepare_model_data(dt, cfg)   # lon/lat, calendar and index year, value, offset, X/Y (km)
```

## Mesh

```{r, eval=params$refit_model}
#| label: fig-fit-mesh
#| fig-cap: "Model mesh and sampling locations in the configured projection."
mesh <- sdmTMB::make_mesh(dt, xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), cutoff = cfg$MESH_CUTOFF_KM)
if (isTRUE(cfg$BARRIER)) {
  ensure_packages("sdmTMBextra")   # installed on demand; see R/0_setup.R
  land <- ggOceanMaps::basemap_data(data = dt, crs = dt_crs)$shapefiles$land
  mesh <- sdmTMBextra::add_barrier_mesh(mesh, land, proj_scaling = 1000)
}
plot_mesh(mesh, crs = dt_crs, data = dt)
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding and refer to @fig-fit-mesh. Confirm caption units, sample size, and interval definitions against the generated result. -->

## Fit

Default formula `value ~ 0 + geartype + s(month) + s(depth)` (temperature off by default). `geartype` stays in when >1 major gear type is present, or whenever a single set gear width is used. `SURVEY_EFFECT: true` adds a cruise-series catchability factor (`fsurvey`), and `CATCHABILITY_TERMS` adds one smooth per catchability covariate (e.g. `hour`); both are predicted at the reference levels set on the grid below.

```{r fit, eval=params$refit_model}
has_multiple_gears <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$geartype) > 1
# `data = dt` sizes the smooth bases to what the survey actually sampled — a series covering
# three months cannot support the default `s(month)` basis and fails with an opaque mgcv error.
form <- build_formula(cfg, has_multiple_gears, data = dt)
form

# Years the survey skipped: an `ar1`/`rw` field assumes evenly spaced steps, and a gap makes
# sdmTMB warn about irregular time spacing and can leave the fit grinding for a very long time.
extra_time <- setdiff(seq(min(dt$year), max(dt$year)), unique(dt$year))

fit <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB(
  form, data = dt, mesh = mesh,
  family = model_family,
  offset = model_offset,   # NULL for EFFORT: density; the column name for EFFORT: offset
  spatial = model_spatial, spatiotemporal = cfg$SPATIOTEMPORAL, time = "year",
  extra_time = if (length(extra_time)) extra_time else NULL,
  control = sdmTMB::sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 2)
)
saveRDS(fit, file.path(out_dir, "model-fit-total.rds"))
```

```{r load-fit, eval=!params$refit_model}
fit <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "model-fit-total.rds"))
```

```{r sanity}
sdmTMB::sanity(fit)
```

`r sanity_sentence(list("The first model" = fit))`

If `sanity()` flags problems (large gradients, non-PD Hessian, range > domain), simplify — coarser mesh, drop a smooth, or change the spatiotemporal structure — rather than pressing on.

## Prediction grid

Depth is extracted per cell and the grid is then trimmed to `MIN_DEPTH`–`MAX_DEPTH`. Never match cells to a bathymetry that was first filtered to a depth band: cells outside the band would inherit the band edge's depth instead of being removed. The table reports cells outside the depth range of the data, where the depth smooth extrapolates.

```{r grid, eval=params$recompute_grid}
region <- make_survey_prediction_region(dt, crs = dt_crs)
grid   <- make_prediction_grid(region, resolution = grid_side_size, max_depth = cfg$MAX_DEPTH)
if (!is.null(cfg$MIN_DEPTH)) grid <- grid[grid$depth >= cfg$MIN_DEPTH, ]
grid   <- tidyr::crossing(as.data.frame(grid), year = sort(unique(dt$year)))
grid$geartype <- levels(factor(dt$geartype))[1]   # reference gear
grid$month    <- 8L                               # reference month
grid <- add_reference_levels(grid, dt, cfg)       # survey and catchability references
# Predict at one unit of swept area, so the prediction is a density and get_index(area =)
# scales it once. Under a Poisson-link family the encounter/positive split at this point is not
# interpretable (one nmi^2 is tens of hauls); only the product is.
grid$log_swept_area <- 0
saveRDS(grid, file.path(out_dir, "prediction-grid.rds"))
```

```{r load-grid, eval=!params$recompute_grid}
grid <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "prediction-grid.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit-depth-range
knitr::kable(
  depth_extrapolation(grid[grid$year == min(grid$year), ], dt),
  caption = "Prediction-grid cells (one year) outside the observed depth range of the data."
)
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding and refer to @tbl-fit-depth-range. Justify any extrapolated cells or trim the grid. -->

## Predict and index

`predict_index()` predicts at offset 0 on the years the model was fitted to and integrates with the grid cell area, so the same call is correct for both effort conventions.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fit-index
#| fig-cap: "Estimated annual index. The line represents the estimate and the shaded interval spans the returned lower and upper limits."
index <- predict_index(fit, grid, area = grid_cell_area_nmi2, bias_correct = params$bias_correct)
pred  <- predict(fit, newdata = grid, return_tmb_object = TRUE)   # for the maps below
saveRDS(index, file.path(out_dir, "index-total.rds"))

ggplot2::ggplot(index, ggplot2::aes(year, est)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Year", y = "Index")
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding and refer to @fig-fit-index. Confirm caption units, sample size, and interval definitions against the generated result. -->

## Absolute scale check

A relative index hides unit errors in the swept area, the offset or the cell area, because they only scale it by a constant. Two checks guard the absolute scale. The **unit ratio** compares the model's density at the sampled hauls (predicted at offset 0) with the observed density there; it does not depend on coverage, so a median outside 1/1.5–1.5 points to a wrong swept-area unit or an offset on the wrong scale. The **design ratio** compares the index with an unstratified swept-area estimate (mean observed density times the grid area); it differs legitimately where the grid includes rarely sampled cells, and only a departure of an order of magnitude suggests a misplaced cell area or tow-distance division.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit-scale-check
density_col <- if (identical(cfg$RESPONSE, "abundance")) "rho_abundance" else "rho_biomass"
grid_area_nmi2 <- grid_cell_area_nmi2 * sum(grid$year == min(grid$year))
scale_check <- check_index_scale(index, dt, total_area = grid_area_nmi2,
                                 density_col = density_col, fit = fit)
if (!isTRUE(scale_check$ok)) warning("Model and observed densities at the hauls differ by a median factor of ",
                                     signif(scale_check$unit_ratio, 3), ". Check the swept-area units and the offset before Step 3.")
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::mutate(scale_check$table, dplyr::across(c(est, design_est, mean_density), signif, 3),
                dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_ratio"), round, 2)),
  caption = "Unit ratio (model / observed density at the hauls) and design ratio (index / unstratified swept-area estimate) per index year."
)
```

<!-- Report both median ratios with inline R from scale_check$unit_ratio and scale_check$design_ratio, and refer to @tbl-fit-scale-check. -->

## Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fig-fit-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics of the first model: residual quantiles, mean predictions, the spatial random field, and fixed effects."
plot_residual_qq(fit)
# A delta model's predict() can return est1/est2 without a combined est column.
if (!"est" %in% names(pred$data)) pred$data$est <- delta_log_density(pred$data, fit)
plot_prediction_map(pred, crs = dt_crs, column = "est", type = "mean")
if ("omega" %in% fitted_fields(fit)) plot_random_field(pred, crs = dt_crs, field = "omega")
plot_fixed_effects(fit)
```

<!-- Describe the supported finding and refer to @fig-fit-diagnostics. Confirm caption units, sample size, and interval definitions against the generated result. -->

If the simple model is sane and the index is plausible, proceed to Step 3 (`index-validate-model`). Record the mesh cutoff, formula, and family in `ai/memory/`.
